[Date]

To: [Plan appeals department and submission address or fax shown on member ID card]  
Re: Quinn Mercado  
Member ID: W696939159  
Reference number: POC-16827CFF67-65871  
Requested service: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion at one cervical interspace  
CPT: 22551  
Date of adverse benefit determination: August 23, 2026

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the adverse benefit determination for the requested C5-C6 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion. Please accept this letter as a request for a first-level internal appeal and a complete reconsideration of the medical necessity of CPT 22551.

The clinical records support the need for surgical treatment:

- I have had 14 months of progressive neck pain that has not improved with rest.
- I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, from April 1, 2026, through July 8, 2026. I completed 18 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for eight months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 13, 2026, produced only three weeks of partial relief.
- MRI of the cervical spine on June 21, 2026, showed a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and compression of the C6 nerve root.
- I have radicular pain and numbness extending into the right thumb and index finger, together with weakness.
- Examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged cervical level.
- The clinical symptoms, examination findings, and MRI findings are anatomically concordant: the C5-C6 lesion compresses the C6 nerve root, and the symptoms and neurologic findings are in the expected C6 distribution.
- Reasonable nonoperative treatment has been attempted for an appropriate duration, including physical therapy, traction, postural training, NSAIDs, and injection therapy, without durable improvement.

These records address the principal medical-necessity issues relevant to this request: persistent and progressive symptoms, failure of substantial conservative treatment, objective imaging demonstrating nerve-root compression, and corresponding neurologic impairment. The limited response to injection therapy further supports that conservative treatment has not provided durable relief.

There are also no documented clinical factors in the submitted records that would independently prevent the requested procedure: there is no active infection or untreated substance use disorder, BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.

I could not locate a publicly available Connecticut Medicaid medical-necessity policy or clinical-criteria document specifically governing CPT 22551, and the denial notice does not identify the policy title, policy number, effective date, or the specific criterion allegedly not satisfied. Therefore, this appeal does not quote or represent any plan policy language. Please provide the exact policy or clinical-review guideline applied to this request, including its title, policy number, effective date, complete criteria for CPT 22551, the specific criterion considered unmet, the clinical rationale for the determination, and the additional information required for approval.

Please reverse the adverse determination and authorize the requested C5-C6 ACDF. If the denial is not reversed, please provide the complete written clinical rationale and all appeal rights. Please also advise whether a peer-to-peer review with Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, is available.

The notice states that the appeal must be received by February 19, 2027. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and identify the reviewer assigned to it.

Sincerely,

Quinn Mercado  
Member ID: W696939159
